sections.answer: Our remote-first UX design agency works in five sectors well represented along the Front Range:
items: SaaS and business-to-business software in Denver, in Boulder, Colorado, and in the Denver Tech Center business district in the south metro, for example onboarding, billing and admin consoles (SaaS UI UX design).
Aerospace and space, for example operator consoles and telemetry views where dense data must stay readable under time pressure.
Outdoor brands and consumer gear companies, for example product finders, fit guides and direct-to-consumer checkout, where we design the digital interface, not the gear (E-commerce UI UX design).
Health systems and digital health, for example patient scheduling and clinician tools (Healthcare UI UX design).
Energy and utilities, including oil and gas and renewables, for example asset monitoring and field-crew apps (data visualization agency).

sections.h2: What can a Denver team hand off to us?
sections.answer: A Denver team can hand off 6 types of UX work to our remote-first UX design agency, either as a full package or as individual pieces that fill a gap in an internal design team.

items.title: User research.
items.body: Conversations with users in each segment, for example trail runners shopping online and the retail staff who advise them.

items.title: UX audit.
items.body: A heuristic usability review plus a Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) check against WCAG 2.2 level AA, with funnel and event data showing where a SaaS trial loses people. Findings are ranked by impact and effort, and the UX audit ends with a prioritized fix roadmap.

items.title: Interface design.
items.body: Card sorts and tree tests reorganize a large catalog or a crowded settings menu before we design the web and app screens.

items.title: Data-dense UI.
items.body: Charts, tables and alert states for engineering consoles where operators scan many values at once.

items.title: Mobile app design.
items.body: iOS and Android flows for field use, with large touch targets and offline states for weak signal.

items.title: Usability testing.
items.body: Moderated remote sessions with 5–8 participants per round for each user group, repeated until critical issues are gone.

sections.h2: Why Denver organizations invest in user experience
sections.answer: Better UX gives Denver organizations four practical gains, and a remote-first UX design agency designs for all four: stronger trial conversion, fewer operator errors, better online sales and shorter onboarding for new staff.

items.title: Converts more trials
items.body: Guided setup and clear pricing pages help SaaS prospects reach value before the trial window closes.

items.title: Prevents operator mistakes
items.body: Distinct alert levels and confirmation steps reduce errors in consoles for aerospace and energy operations.

items.title: Lifts online sales
items.body: Better product discovery and fit guidance help outdoor gear shoppers buy with confidence and return less.

items.title: Shortens staff onboarding
items.body: Internal tools built on one design system, a shared set of components and usage rules, let new hires learn one pattern instead of a dozen legacy screens.

sections.h2: What are the stages of a Denver UX engagement?
sections.answer: A research and design sprint with our remote-first UX design agency takes 4–8 weeks from first call to developer handoff and unfolds in 5 stages, with 2–4 designers and every review held inside Mountain Time hours.

items.title: Framing call (1–2 days)
items.body: We define the problem, the users, the metric that will show success and the constraints on scope and timing.

items.title: Learn from users (5–10 days)
items.body: User interviews, analytics and an expert review are synthesized into a short list of opportunities ranked by impact.

items.title: Shape the solution (2–3 days)
items.body: Remote working sessions with product and engineering choose a direction; on-site workshops on the Front Range can be added for larger engagements.

items.title: Design in detail (10–20 days)
items.body: We produce the user flows, polished interface screens and an interactive prototype in Figma, sharing progress twice a week.

items.title: Prove and ship (5–10 days)
items.body: A final usability testing round with real users confirms the design, and annotated specs, tokens and components move to your engineers.

sections.h2: What is the price of UX design for a Denver product?
sections.answer: Our remote-first UX design agency prices a focused 2–3 week UX audit at $5,000–$15,000 and a 4–8 week research and design sprint at $25,000–$60,000. The final number depends on the number of journeys, the platforms involved, the depth of user research and whether a design system is part of the work.
sections.body: Complete product redesigns with a design system run $60,000–$180,000 across 8–16 weeks, and an embedded design team costs $15,000–$40,000 per month. Startups and enterprises get the same process from a UX agency Denver companies can hire instead of building an in-house design team: every project begins with a free consultation and a fixed-scope proposal. Compare UX audit services and usability testing services.

sections.h2: Questions Denver teams ask a UX agency
sections.answer: Our remote-first UX/UI design company answers six questions Front Range product leaders can ask before they buy Denver UI/UX design services.

faqs.a: No. We are a remote-first UX design agency with no Denver or Colorado office. Denver teams work with us over video on an Eastern Time schedule from our Reston, Virginia headquarters, and we travel to the Front Range for on-site workshops on larger projects.

faqs.q: Do UX/UI services in Denver need a local office?
faqs.a: No. A Denver UX agency does not need a local office when it shares your working hours. As a remote-first UX agency Denver teams can book within their own working day, we work an Eastern Time schedule from Reston, Virginia, with 6–7 hours of daily overlap with Mountain Time. The UX design Denver teams buy from us is research-led: user research, interface design and usability testing, priced as fixed-scope engagements from $5,000.

faqs.q: Can you design for users working outdoors or in the field?
faqs.a: Yes. We design interfaces for field crews and outdoor gear users who face glare, gloves, cold and patchy connectivity, with high-contrast UI, large touch targets and offline states, and can add on-site contextual inquiry when field conditions matter. Our UX research services explain how that user research is planned.

faqs.q: Do you work with Boulder startups?
faqs.a: Yes. Early-stage teams in Boulder and Denver, Colorado, can start with a $25,000–$60,000 sprint to shape a minimum viable product or fix onboarding before a funding round. The designers who run the user research stay through design and usability testing.

faqs.q: Can you handle technical aerospace or energy interfaces?
faqs.a: Yes. We work closely with your subject-matter experts, learn the domain vocabulary, and structure dense data so operators find the critical value first. Before handoff, we check the console design with your operators in usability testing sessions.

faqs.q: How soon can a Denver UX project start?
faqs.a: A Denver UX project with us starts 1–2 weeks after proposal approval, beginning with a framing call and a user research plan. A sprint ends with research findings, Figma files, an interactive prototype tested with real users, and annotated specs and components; a UX audit ends with a prioritized fix roadmap.
